declarations.statement:
lemma angularVelocity_eq (M : RigidBodyMotion 3) (t : Time) :
    M.angularVelocity t = crossProductVee (M.angularVelocityTensor t)

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.crossProductMatrix_angularVelocity
declarations.doc:
The hat map recovers the angular velocity tensor from the angular velocity vector, `[ω]ₓ = Ω`.
This is the defining relationship between the vector and tensor forms of the angular velocity in
three dimensions; it holds because `Ω` is skew-symmetric.
declarations.statement:
lemma crossProductMatrix_angularVelocity (M : RigidBodyMotion 3) (t : Time)
    (hR : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t) :
    crossProductMatrix (M.angularVelocity t) = M.angularVelocityTensor t

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.angularVelocity_of_orientation_const
declarations.doc: A rigid body whose orientation is constant in time has zero angular velocity vector.
declarations.statement:
lemma angularVelocity_of_orientation_const (M : RigidBodyMotion 3)
    (R : Matrix.specialOrthogonalGroup (Fin 3) ℝ) (h : M.orientation = fun _ => R) :
    M.angularVelocity = 0

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.angularVelocityTensor_mul_orientation
declarations.doc:
The time derivative of the orientation is `Ṙ = Ω R`, recovering the orientation path from its
angular velocity tensor `Ω = Ṙ Rᵀ` via the orthogonality `Rᵀ R = 1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma angularVelocityTensor_mul_orientation (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) :
    M.angularVelocityTensor t * (M.orientation t).1 = ∂ₜ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.deriv_orientation_mulVec_eq_angularVelocity_cross
declarations.doc:
The rotational part of the velocity of the body point `y` is the cross product of the
angular velocity with the point's position relative to the centre of mass:
`Ṙ(t) (y − c) = ω(t) × (displacement t y − comTrajectory t)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_orientation_mulVec_eq_angularVelocity_cross (M : RigidBodyMotion 3) (y : Space 3)
    (t : Time) (hR : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t) :
    ∂ₜ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t *ᵥ (fun j => y j - M.centerOfMass j)
      = M.angularVelocity t ⨯₃ fun j => M.displacement t y j - M.comTrajectory t j

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.velocity_eq_angularVelocity
declarations.doc:
The Landau–Lifshitz velocity decomposition `v = V + ω × r` for a rigid body in three
dimensions: the velocity of a body point is the centre-of-mass velocity plus the cross product of
the angular velocity with the point's position relative to the centre of mass.
declarations.statement:
theorem velocity_eq_angularVelocity (M : RigidBodyMotion 3) (y : Space 3) (t : Time) (i : Fin 3)
    (hR : Differentiable ℝ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1)) (hX : Differentiable ℝ M.comTrajectory) :
    M.velocity y t i = M.centerOfMassVelocity t i
        + (M.angularVelocity t ⨯₃ fun j => M.displacement t y j - M.comTrajectory t j) i

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.bodyAngularVelocityTensor
declarations.doc:
The body-frame (co-rotating) angular velocity tensor `Ω_body(t) = R(t)ᵀ Ṙ(t)` of a rigid body
in motion, where `R(t) = orientation t`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def bodyAngularVelocityTensor (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) :
    Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.bodyAngularVelocityTensor_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma bodyAngularVelocityTensor_eq (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) :
    M.bodyAngularVelocityTensor t = ((M.orientation t).1)ᵀ * ∂ₜ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.orientation_mul_bodyAngularVelocityTensor
declarations.doc:
The time derivative of the orientation is `Ṙ = R Ω_body`, recovering the orientation path from
its body-frame angular velocity tensor via the orthogonality `R Rᵀ = 1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma orientation_mul_bodyAngularVelocityTensor (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) :
    (M.orientation t).1 * M.bodyAngularVelocityTensor t = ∂ₜ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.angularVelocityTensor_eq_orientation_conj
declarations.doc:
The spatial tensor is the body-frame tensor rotated into the inertial frame,
`Ω = R Ω_body Rᵀ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma angularVelocityTensor_eq_orientation_conj (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) :
    M.angularVelocityTensor t
      = (M.orientation t).1 * M.bodyAngularVelocityTensor t * ((M.orientation t).1)ᵀ

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.bodyAngularVelocityTensor_eq_orientation_conj
declarations.doc:
The body-frame tensor is the spatial tensor conjugated into the body frame,
`Ω_body = Rᵀ Ω R`.
declarations.statement:
lemma bodyAngularVelocityTensor_eq_orientation_conj (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) :
    M.bodyAngularVelocityTensor t
      = ((M.orientation t).1)ᵀ * M.angularVelocityTensor t * (M.orientation t).1

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.bodyAngularVelocityTensor_transpose
declarations.doc:
The body-frame angular velocity tensor is skew-symmetric, `Ω_bodyᵀ = -Ω_body`: it lies in the
Lie algebra `𝔰𝔬(d)`, inherited from the spatial tensor by conjugation.
declarations.statement:
lemma bodyAngularVelocityTensor_transpose (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time)
    (hR : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t) :
    (M.bodyAngularVelocityTensor t)ᵀ = - M.bodyAngularVelocityTensor t

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.bodyAngularVelocity
declarations.doc:
The body-frame angular velocity *vector* `ω_body(t)` of a rigid body moving in three-dimensional
space: the vector dual to the body-frame angular velocity tensor `Ω_body(t)` under the hat map,
`ω_body = Ω_bodyᵛ`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def bodyAngularVelocity (M : RigidBodyMotion 3) (t : Time) : Fin 3 → ℝ

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.bodyAngularVelocity_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma bodyAngularVelocity_eq (M : RigidBodyMotion 3) (t : Time) :
    M.bodyAngularVelocity t = crossProductVee (M.bodyAngularVelocityTensor t)

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.crossProductMatrix_bodyAngularVelocity
declarations.doc:
The hat map recovers the body-frame angular velocity tensor from the body-frame angular
velocity vector, `[ω_body]ₓ = Ω_body`; it holds because `Ω_body` is skew-symmetric.
declarations.statement:
lemma crossProductMatrix_bodyAngularVelocity (M : RigidBodyMotion 3) (t : Time)
    (hR : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t) :
    crossProductMatrix (M.bodyAngularVelocity t) = M.bodyAngularVelocityTensor t

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.bodyAngularVelocityTensor_of_orientation_const
declarations.doc:
A rigid body whose orientation is constant in time has zero body-frame angular velocity
tensor.
declarations.statement:
lemma bodyAngularVelocityTensor_of_orientation_const (M : RigidBodyMotion d)
    (R : Matrix.specialOrthogonalGroup (Fin d) ℝ) (h : M.orientation = fun _ => R) :
    M.bodyAngularVelocityTensor = 0

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.bodyAngularVelocity_of_orientation_const
declarations.doc:
A rigid body whose orientation is constant in time has zero body-frame angular velocity
vector.
declarations.statement:
lemma bodyAngularVelocity_of_orientation_const (M : RigidBodyMotion 3)
    (R : Matrix.specialOrthogonalGroup (Fin 3) ℝ) (h : M.orientation = fun _ => R) :
    M.bodyAngularVelocity = 0

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.deriv_orientation_mulVec_eq_orientation_bodyAngularVelocity_cross
declarations.doc:
The rotational velocity written through the body-frame angular velocity,
`Ṙ(t) v = R(t) (ω_body(t) × v)`: the derivative of the orientation acts as the body-frame angular
velocity `ω_body` crossed with `v`, rotated back into the inertial frame by `R`.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_orientation_mulVec_eq_orientation_bodyAngularVelocity_cross (M : RigidBodyMotion 3)
    (v : Fin 3 → ℝ) (t : Time)
    (hR : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t) :
    ∂ₜ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t *ᵥ v
      = (M.orientation t).1 *ᵥ (M.bodyAngularVelocity t ⨯₃ v)

modules.title: Rigid bodies
modules.doc:
A rigid body is one where the distance and relative orientation between particles does not change.
In other words, the body remains undeformed.

In this module we will define the basic properties of a rigid body, including
- mass
- center of mass
- inertia tensor
- inertia tensor about an arbitrary point

The moments of the last are taken about the given point rather than about the origin of the
reference frame. The parallel-axis theorem expresses it in terms of the inertia tensor about the
centre of mass.

## References

* Landau and Lifshitz, Mechanics, page 100, Section 32. [ref: landau_mechanics]

declarations.name: RigidBody
declarations.doc: A Rigid body defined by its mass distribution.
declarations.statement:
structure RigidBody (d : ℕ) where
  /-- The mass distribution of the rigid body. -/
  ρ : C^⊤⟮𝓘(ℝ, Space d), Space d; 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ), ℝ⟯ →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ

declarations.name: RigidBody.mass
declarations.doc: The total mass of the rigid body.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def mass {d : ℕ} (R : RigidBody d) : ℝ

declarations.name: RigidBody.rho_one
declarations.doc: The mass distribution applied to the constant function `1` is the total mass.
declarations.statement:
lemma rho_one {d : ℕ} (R : RigidBody d) :
    R.ρ (1 : C^⊤⟮𝓘(ℝ, Space d), Space d; 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ), ℝ⟯) = R.mass

declarations.name: RigidBody.centerOfMass
declarations.doc: The center of mass of the rigid body.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def centerOfMass {d : ℕ} (R : RigidBody d) : Space d

declarations.name: RigidBody.inertiaTensor
declarations.doc: The inertia tensor of the rigid body.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def inertiaTensor {d : ℕ} (R : RigidBody d) :
    Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ

declarations.name: RigidBody.inertiaTensor_symmetric
declarations.statement:
lemma inertiaTensor_symmetric {d : ℕ} (R : RigidBody d) (i j : Fin d) :
    R.inertiaTensor i j = R.inertiaTensor j i

declarations.name: RigidBody.rho_coord_sub_centerOfMass
declarations.doc:
The first moment of the mass distribution about its own centre of mass vanishes:
for nonzero mass, `ρ` of the centred `j`-th coordinate function is zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma rho_coord_sub_centerOfMass {d : ℕ} (R : RigidBody d) (h : R.mass ≠ 0) (j : Fin d) :
    R.ρ (cmap (fun y => y j - R.centerOfMass j) (by fun_prop)) = 0

declarations.name: RigidBody.inertiaTensorAbout
declarations.doc:
The inertia tensor of the rigid body about the point `p`, that is with the moments taken
about `p` rather than about the origin of the reference frame. Taking `p` to be the origin
recovers `RigidBody.inertiaTensor`, see `RigidBody.inertiaTensorAbout_zero`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def inertiaTensorAbout {d : ℕ} (R : RigidBody d) (p : Space d) :
    Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ

declarations.name: RigidBody.inertiaTensorAbout_apply
declarations.doc: The `(i, j)` entry of the inertia tensor about `p` as a moment of the mass distribution.
declarations.statement:
lemma inertiaTensorAbout_apply {d : ℕ} (R : RigidBody d) (p : Space d) (i j : Fin d) :
    R.inertiaTensorAbout p i j = R.ρ (cmap (fun y => (if i = j then 1 else 0) *
      ∑ k : Fin d, (y k - p k) ^ 2 - (y i - p i) * (y j - p j)) (by fun_prop))

declarations.name: RigidBody.inertiaTensorAbout_zero
declarations.doc: The inertia tensor about the origin is the inertia tensor.
declarations.statement:
lemma inertiaTensorAbout_zero {d : ℕ} (R : RigidBody d) :
    R.inertiaTensorAbout 0 = R.inertiaTensor

declarations.name: RigidBody.inertiaTensorAbout_symmetric
declarations.doc: The inertia tensor about any point is symmetric.
declarations.statement:
lemma inertiaTensorAbout_symmetric {d : ℕ} (R : RigidBody d) (p : Space d) (i j : Fin d) :
    R.inertiaTensorAbout p i j = R.inertiaTensorAbout p j i

declarations.name: RigidBody.inertiaTensorAbout_integrand_split
declarations.doc:
The integrand of the inertia tensor about `p` splits into the integrand about the centre of
mass, terms linear in the centred coordinates `y − c`, and a constant built from the
displacement `c − p`.
declarations.statement:
lemma inertiaTensorAbout_integrand_split {d : ℕ} (R : RigidBody d) (p : Space d) (i j : Fin d) :
    cmap (fun y => (if i = j then 1 else 0) * ∑ k : Fin d, (y k - p k) ^ 2
        - (y i - p i) * (y j - p j)) (by fun_prop)
      = cmap (fun y => (if i = j then 1 else 0) * ∑ k : Fin d, (y k - R.centerOfMass k) ^ 2
            - (y i - R.centerOfMass i) * (y j - R.centerOfMass j)) (by fun_prop)
        + ∑ k : Fin d, (2 * (if i = j then 1 else 0) * (R.centerOfMass k - p k)) •
            cmap (fun y => y k - R.centerOfMass k) (by fun_prop)
        - (R.centerOfMass j - p j) • cmap (fun y => y i - R.centerOfMass i) (by fun_prop)
        - (R.centerOfMass i - p i) • cmap (fun y => y j - R.centerOfMass j) (by fun_prop)
        + ((if i = j then 1 else 0) * ∑ k : Fin d, (R.centerOfMass k - p k) ^ 2
            - (R.centerOfMass i - p i) * (R.centerOfMass j - p j)) •
          (1 : C^⊤⟮𝓘(ℝ, Space d), Space d; 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ), ℝ⟯)

declarations.name: RigidBody.inertiaTensorAbout_eq_centerOfMass_add_pointMass
declarations.doc:
**The parallel-axis theorem**: the inertia tensor about a point `p` is the inertia tensor
about the centre of mass `c` plus the inertia tensor about `p` of a point particle carrying the
total mass of the body and sitting at `c`, that is `M (|c − p|² 1 − (c − p) ⊗ (c − p))`.
declarations.statement:
theorem inertiaTensorAbout_eq_centerOfMass_add_pointMass {d : ℕ} (R : RigidBody d) (h : R.mass ≠ 0)
    (p : Space d) :
    R.inertiaTensorAbout p = R.inertiaTensorAbout R.centerOfMass
      + R.mass • (⟪R.centerOfMass - p, R.centerOfMass - p⟫_ℝ • (1 : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ)
        - Matrix.vecMulVec ⇑(R.centerOfMass - p) ⇑(R.centerOfMass - p))

declarations.name: RigidBody.inertiaTensor_eq_centerOfMass_add_pointMass
declarations.doc:
The inertia tensor about the origin is the inertia tensor about the centre of mass `c` plus
`M (|c|² 1 − c ⊗ c)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma inertiaTensor_eq_centerOfMass_add_pointMass {d : ℕ} (R : RigidBody d) (h : R.mass ≠ 0) :
    R.inertiaTensor = R.inertiaTensorAbout R.centerOfMass
      + R.mass • (⟪R.centerOfMass, R.centerOfMass⟫_ℝ • (1 : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ)
        - Matrix.vecMulVec ⇑R.centerOfMass ⇑R.centerOfMass)

modules.title: Kinetic energy of a rigid body
modules.doc:
For a rigid body rotating with angular velocity `ω` about its reference point the point at
position `r` has velocity `ω × r`, so its kinetic energy is `T = ½ ∫ |ω × r|² dm`. Since
`|ω × r|² = ω · (r × (ω × r))` and the angular momentum is `L = ∫ r × (ω × r) dm = I ω`, the
kinetic energy is the quadratic form `T = ½ ω · L = ½ ω · I ω` in the inertia tensor.

For a rigid body in motion the total kinetic energy is the mass integral of half the squared
speed of its points, `T = ½ ∫ ⟪v, v⟫ dm`. König's theorem splits it into the kinetic energy of
the centre of mass plus the rotational energy about the centre of mass,
`T = ½ M ⟪V, V⟫ + ½ ∫ |Ṙ (y − c)|² dm`: the cross term vanishes because the first moment of the
mass distribution about its centre of mass is zero. In three dimensions the rotational term is
`½ ∫ |ω × r|² dm`, with `ω` the angular velocity vector and `r` the position of the body point
relative to the centre of mass.

The total kinetic energy is defined with the point velocity taken in the closed form
`Ṙ(t) (y − c) + V(t)` (`velocityClosedForm`), which is polynomial in the body point and hence
smooth for any motion; for differentiable motions it agrees with the honest point velocity
`∂ₜ (displacement · y)`, recovering `T = ½ ∫ ⟪v, v⟫ dm` (`kineticEnergy_eq_integral_velocity`).

## References

* Landau and Lifshitz, Mechanics, Section 32. [ref: landau_mechanics]

declarations.name: RigidBody.rotationalKineticEnergy
declarations.doc:
The rotational kinetic energy of a rigid body rotating with angular velocity `ω` about its
reference point: half the contraction of `ω` with the inertia tensor, `T = ½ ω · (I ω)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def rotationalKineticEnergy (R : RigidBody 3) (ω : Fin 3 → ℝ) : ℝ

declarations.name: RigidBody.rotationalKineticEnergy_eq_angularMomentum
declarations.doc:
The rotational kinetic energy is half the contraction of the angular velocity with the angular
momentum: `T = ½ ω · L`.
declarations.statement:
lemma rotationalKineticEnergy_eq_angularMomentum (R : RigidBody 3) (ω : Fin 3 → ℝ) :
    R.rotationalKineticEnergy ω = (1 / (2 : ℝ)) * (ω ⬝ᵥ R.angularMomentum ω)

declarations.name: RigidBody.rotationalKineticEnergy_eq_integral
declarations.doc:
The rotational kinetic energy equals the mass integral of the local rotational speed squared:
`T = ½ ∫ |ω × r|² dm`.
declarations.statement:
theorem rotationalKineticEnergy_eq_integral (R : RigidBody 3) (ω : Fin 3 → ℝ) :
    R.rotationalKineticEnergy ω
      = (1 / (2 : ℝ)) * R.ρ ⟨fun x => (ω ⨯₃ (x : Fin 3 → ℝ)) ⬝ᵥ (ω ⨯₃ (x : Fin 3 → ℝ)),
        ContDiff.contMDiff <| (contDiff_cross_dotProduct_cross ω).comp
          (contDiff_pi.mpr fun i => Space.eval_contDiff i)⟩

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.kineticEnergy
declarations.doc:
The total kinetic energy of a rigid body in motion at time `t`: half the mass integral of the
squared speed of the body points, `T = ½ ∫ ⟪v, v⟫ dm`, with the point velocity taken in the
closed form `velocityClosedForm`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def kineticEnergy {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) : ℝ

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.kineticEnergy_eq_integral_velocity
declarations.doc:
For a differentiable motion the integrand of `kineticEnergy` is the squared speed of the
honest point velocity: `T = ½ ∫ ⟪v, v⟫ dm` with `v = ∂ₜ (displacement · y)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma kineticEnergy_eq_integral_velocity {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time)
    (hR : Differentiable ℝ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1))
    (hX : Differentiable ℝ M.comTrajectory) :
    M.kineticEnergy t = (1 / (2 : ℝ)) * M.ρ (cmap
      (fun y => (⟪M.velocity y t, M.velocity y t⟫_ℝ))
      (by
        simp only [← M.velocityClosedForm_eq_velocity t hR hX]
        exact M.contDiff_velocityClosedForm_inner t))

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.kineticEnergy_integrand_split
declarations.doc:
The squared-speed integrand of `kineticEnergy` splits into the squared rotational speed
`|Ṙ (y − c)|²`, a term linear in the body-frame coordinate `y − c`, and the constant squared
centre-of-mass speed `⟪V, V⟫`.
declarations.statement:
lemma kineticEnergy_integrand_split {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) :
    cmap (fun y => (⟪M.velocityClosedForm t y, M.velocityClosedForm t y⟫_ℝ))
        (M.contDiff_velocityClosedForm_inner t)
      = cmap (fun y =>
            (∂ₜ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t *ᵥ fun j => y j - M.centerOfMass j) ⬝ᵥ
            (∂ₜ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t *ᵥ fun j => y j - M.centerOfMass j))
          (by simp only [dotProduct, Matrix.mulVec]; fun_prop)
        + ∑ j, (2 * (((M.centerOfMassVelocity t : Fin d → ℝ) ᵥ*
              ∂ₜ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t) j)) •
            cmap (fun y => y j - M.centerOfMass j) (by fun_prop)
        + (⟪M.centerOfMassVelocity t, M.centerOfMassVelocity t⟫_ℝ) •
            (1 : C^⊤⟮𝓘(ℝ, Space d), Space d; 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ), ℝ⟯)

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.kineticEnergy_eq_translational_add_rotational
declarations.doc:
**König's theorem**, general form: the total kinetic energy of a rigid body in motion splits
into the kinetic energy of the centre of mass plus the rotational energy about the centre of
mass, `T = ½ M ⟪V, V⟫ + ½ ∫ |Ṙ (y − c)|² dm`.
declarations.statement:
theorem kineticEnergy_eq_translational_add_rotational {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time)
    (h : M.mass ≠ 0) :
    M.kineticEnergy t
      = (1 / (2 : ℝ)) * M.mass * (⟪M.centerOfMassVelocity t, M.centerOfMassVelocity t⟫_ℝ)
        + (1 / (2 : ℝ)) * M.ρ (cmap (fun y =>
            (∂ₜ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t *ᵥ fun j => y j - M.centerOfMass j) ⬝ᵥ
            (∂ₜ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t *ᵥ fun j => y j - M.centerOfMass j))
          (by simp only [dotProduct, Matrix.mulVec]; fun_prop))

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.kineticEnergy_eq_translational_add_angularVelocity
declarations.doc:
**König's theorem** in three dimensions: the total kinetic energy of a rigid body in motion
splits as `T = ½ M ⟪V, V⟫ + ½ ∫ |ω × r|² dm`, with `ω` the angular velocity vector and
`r = displacement − comTrajectory` the position of the body point relative to the centre of
mass.
declarations.statement:
theorem kineticEnergy_eq_translational_add_angularVelocity (M : RigidBodyMotion 3) (t : Time)
    (h : M.mass ≠ 0) (hR : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t) :
    M.kineticEnergy t
      = (1 / (2 : ℝ)) * M.mass * (⟪M.centerOfMassVelocity t, M.centerOfMassVelocity t⟫_ℝ)
        + (1 / (2 : ℝ)) * M.ρ (cmap (fun y =>
            (M.angularVelocity t ⨯₃ fun j => M.displacement t y j - M.comTrajectory t j) ⬝ᵥ
            (M.angularVelocity t ⨯₃ fun j => M.displacement t y j - M.comTrajectory t j))
          (by
            exact (contDiff_cross_dotProduct_cross (M.angularVelocity t)).comp
              (contDiff_pi.mpr fun j =>
                ((Space.eval_contDiff j).comp (M.displacement_contDiff t)).sub
                  contDiff_const)))

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.kineticEnergy_eq_translational_add_bodyAngularVelocity
declarations.doc:
**König's theorem** in the body frame. The total kinetic energy `M.kineticEnergy t`, formed from
the lab-frame point velocities, splits at the centre of mass (`centerOfMass = 0`) as
`T = ½ M ⟪V, V⟫ + rotationalKineticEnergy ω_body`. The rotational energy is a frame-independent
scalar, so it is evaluated here from the *body-frame* angular velocity `ω_body`: the spatial form
`|Ṙ (y − c)|²` and the body form `|ω_body × (y − c)|²` agree because
`Ṙ (y − c) = R (ω_body × (y − c))` and `R`, being orthogonal, preserves the norm.
declarations.statement:
theorem kineticEnergy_eq_translational_add_bodyAngularVelocity (M : RigidBodyMotion 3) (t : Time)
    (h : M.mass ≠ 0) (hR : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t)
    (hc : M.centerOfMass = 0) :
    M.kineticEnergy t
      = (1 / (2 : ℝ)) * M.mass * (⟪M.centerOfMassVelocity t, M.centerOfMassVelocity t⟫_ℝ)
        + M.toRigidBody.rotationalKineticEnergy (M.bodyAngularVelocity t)

modules.title: Rigid body motion
modules.doc:
The static `RigidBody` records a body-fixed mass distribution. To describe a rigid body *in
motion* we record, in addition, the trajectory of its centre of mass in the inertial frame and the
body's time-dependent orientation (a rotation about the centre of mass).

From this configuration we define the velocity of the centre of mass and the body's linear
momentum. The reference point is taken to be the centre of mass, following the decomposition of
a rigid motion into a translation of the centre of mass plus a rotation about it.

## References

* Landau and Lifshitz, Mechanics, Section 32. [ref: landau_mechanics]

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion
declarations.doc:
A motion of a rigid body in `d`-dimensional space: the body together with the inertial-frame
trajectory of its centre of mass and its time-dependent orientation (a rotation about the centre
of mass).
declarations.statement:
structure RigidBodyMotion (d : ℕ) extends RigidBody d where
  /-- The position of the centre of mass in the inertial frame as a function of time. -/
  comTrajectory : Time → Space d
  /-- The orientation of the body, a rotation about the centre of mass, as a function of time. -/
  orientation : Time → Matrix.specialOrthogonalGroup (Fin d) ℝ

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.orientation_mul_transpose
declarations.doc: The orientation matrix is special orthogonal, so `R Rᵀ = 1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma orientation_mul_transpose {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) :
    (M.orientation t).1 * ((M.orientation t).1)ᵀ = 1

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.centerOfMassVelocity
declarations.doc:
The velocity of the centre of mass of a rigid body in motion, defined as the time-derivative
of its centre-of-mass trajectory. This is the velocity `V` in the Landau–Lifshitz decomposition
`v = V + Ω × r` of the velocity of a point of the body.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def centerOfMassVelocity {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) :
    Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.centerOfMassVelocity_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma centerOfMassVelocity_eq {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) :
    M.centerOfMassVelocity = ∂ₜᵥ M.comTrajectory

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.centerOfMassVelocity_of_comTrajectory_const
declarations.doc: A rigid body whose centre of mass is stationary has zero centre-of-mass velocity.
declarations.statement:
lemma centerOfMassVelocity_of_comTrajectory_const {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (c : Space d)
    (h : M.comTrajectory = fun _ => c) : M.centerOfMassVelocity = 0

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.linearMomentum
declarations.doc:
The linear momentum of a rigid body in motion: the total mass times the velocity of the
centre of mass.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def linearMomentum {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) :
    Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.linearMomentum_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma linearMomentum_eq {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) :
    M.linearMomentum = fun t => M.mass • M.centerOfMassVelocity t

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.displacement
declarations.doc:
The rigid displacement carrying the body frame into the inertial frame at time `t`: the
rotation `orientation t` about the centre of mass, followed by the translation placing the centre
of mass at `comTrajectory t`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def displacement {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) : Space d → Space d

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.displacement_apply
declarations.doc: The `k`-th coordinate of the rigid displacement applied to `y`.
declarations.statement:
lemma displacement_apply {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) (y : Space d) (k : Fin d) :
    M.displacement t y k =
      (∑ j, (M.orientation t).val k j * (y j - M.centerOfMass j)) + M.comTrajectory t k

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.displacement_contDiff
declarations.statement:
lemma displacement_contDiff {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) :
    ContDiff ℝ ⊤ (M.displacement t)

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.orientation_mulVec_sub_centerOfMass
declarations.doc:
Rotating the body-frame position of `y` relative to the centre of mass gives its
inertial-frame position relative to the moving centre of mass:
`R(t) (y − c) = displacement t y − comTrajectory t`.
declarations.statement:
lemma orientation_mulVec_sub_centerOfMass {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time)
    (y : Space d) :
    (M.orientation t).1 *ᵥ (fun j => y j - M.centerOfMass j)
      = fun j => M.displacement t y j - M.comTrajectory t j

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.massDistribution
declarations.doc:
The mass distribution of the rigid body in motion at time `t`: the pushforward of the
body-fixed mass distribution along the rigid displacement, acting on a test function `f` by
`f ↦ ρ (f ∘ displacement t)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def massDistribution {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) : RigidBody d

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.massDistribution_mass
declarations.doc:
The motion preserves the total mass: the mass distribution at any time `t` has the same total
mass as the body.
declarations.statement:
lemma massDistribution_mass {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) :
    (M.massDistribution t).mass = M.mass

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.massDistribution_centerOfMass
declarations.doc:
The centre of mass of the moving mass distribution tracks the prescribed trajectory: for a
body of nonzero mass, the centre of mass of `massDistribution M t` is exactly `comTrajectory t`.
This is the decisive check that `comTrajectory` and `orientation` are wired correctly in
`RigidBodyMotion`.
declarations.statement:
lemma massDistribution_centerOfMass {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) (h : M.mass ≠ 0) :
    (M.massDistribution t).centerOfMass = M.comTrajectory t

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.velocity
declarations.doc:
The velocity of the material point `y` of a rigid body in motion: the inertial-frame time
derivative of the trajectory `s ↦ displacement s y` of that point.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def velocity {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (y : Space d) :
    Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.velocity_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma velocity_eq {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (y : Space d) (t : Time) :
    M.velocity y t = ∂ₜᵥ (fun s => M.displacement s y) t

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.velocity_apply
declarations.doc:
The `i`-th component of the velocity of a body point is the time derivative of the `i`-th
coordinate of its inertial-frame trajectory.
declarations.statement:
lemma velocity_apply {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (y : Space d) (t : Time) (i : Fin d)
    (hd : Differentiable ℝ (fun s => M.displacement s y)) :
    M.velocity y t i = ∂ₜ (fun s => M.displacement s y i) t

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.velocity_centerOfMass
declarations.doc:
The material point at the centre of mass moves with the centre-of-mass velocity, for any
motion: `v(centreOfMass) = V`. This is the velocity counterpart of `massDistribution_centerOfMass`.
declarations.statement:
lemma velocity_centerOfMass {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) :
    M.velocity M.centerOfMass = M.centerOfMassVelocity

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.velocity_of_orientation_const
declarations.doc:
A rigid body in pure translation (constant orientation) has every point moving with the
centre-of-mass velocity: `v = V`.
declarations.statement:
lemma velocity_of_orientation_const {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (y : Space d)
    (R : Matrix.specialOrthogonalGroup (Fin d) ℝ) (h : M.orientation = fun _ => R) :
    M.velocity y = M.centerOfMassVelocity

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.velocity_eq_deriv_orientation
declarations.doc:
The velocity of a body point decomposes as `v = Ṙ (y − c) + V`: the rate of change of the
orientation acting on the body-frame position, plus the centre-of-mass velocity.
declarations.statement:
lemma velocity_eq_deriv_orientation {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (y : Space d) (t : Time)
    (i : Fin d) (hR : Differentiable ℝ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1))
    (hX : Differentiable ℝ M.comTrajectory) :
    M.velocity y t i
      = (∂ₜ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t *ᵥ fun j => y j - M.centerOfMass j) i
        + M.centerOfMassVelocity t i

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.velocityClosedForm
declarations.doc:
The closed form `Ṙ(t) (y − c) + V(t)` of the velocity of the body point `y` at time `t`.
Unlike `velocity` — whose junk values on non-differentiable motions need not vary continuously
with `y` — it is polynomial in `y` for any motion, so its squared speed can be bundled as the
smooth integrand of the total kinetic energy; for differentiable motions the two agree, see
`velocityClosedForm_eq_velocity`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def velocityClosedForm {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) (y : Space d) :
    EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.velocityClosedForm_apply
declarations.doc: The `i`-th coordinate of the closed-form velocity.
declarations.statement:
lemma velocityClosedForm_apply {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) (y : Space d)
    (i : Fin d) :
    M.velocityClosedForm t y i
      = (∂ₜ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t *ᵥ fun j => y j - M.centerOfMass j) i
        + M.centerOfMassVelocity t i

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.velocityClosedForm_val
declarations.doc: The closed-form velocity as a plain vector-valued function of the coordinates of `y`.
declarations.statement:
lemma velocityClosedForm_val {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) (y : Space d) :
    (M.velocityClosedForm t y : Fin d → ℝ)
      = (∂ₜ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t *ᵥ fun j => y j - M.centerOfMass j)
        + (M.centerOfMassVelocity t : Fin d → ℝ)

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.velocityClosedForm_eq_velocity
declarations.doc: For a differentiable motion the closed-form velocity is the honest point velocity.
declarations.statement:
lemma velocityClosedForm_eq_velocity {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time)
    (hR : Differentiable ℝ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1))
    (hX : Differentiable ℝ M.comTrajectory) (y : Space d) :
    M.velocityClosedForm t y = M.velocity y t

declarations.name: RigidBodyMotion.contDiff_velocityClosedForm_inner
declarations.doc: The squared speed of a body point, in closed form, is a smooth function of the point.
declarations.statement:
lemma contDiff_velocityClosedForm_inner {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) :
    ContDiff ℝ ⊤ fun y : Space d => (⟪M.velocityClosedForm t y, M.velocityClosedForm t y⟫_ℝ)

modules.title: The solid sphere as a rigid body

declarations.name: RigidBody.solidSphere
declarations.doc: The solid sphere as a rigid body.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def solidSphere (d : ℕ) (m R : ℝ≥0) : RigidBody d

declarations.name: RigidBody.solidSphere_mass
declarations.statement: lemma solidSphere_mass {d : ℕ} (m R : ℝ≥0) (hr : R ≠ 0) : (solidSphere d m R).mass = m

declarations.name: RigidBody.solidSphere_centerOfMass
declarations.doc: The center of mass of a solid sphere located at the origin is `0`.
declarations.statement: lemma solidSphere_centerOfMass {d : ℕ} (m R : ℝ≥0) : (solidSphere d m R).centerOfMass = 0

modules.title: Wave equation
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this module we define the wave equation in `d`-dimensional Euclidean space,
and prove that plane waves are solutions to the wave equation.
By a plne wave we mean a function of the form `f(t, x) = f₀(⟪x, s⟫_ℝ - c * t)` where
`s` is a direction vector and `c` is the propagation speed.

## ii. Key results

- `WaveEquation`: The general form of the wave equation where `c` is the propagation speed.
- `planeWave`: A vector-valued plane wave travelling in the direction of `s` with
  propagation speed `c`.
- `planeWave_waveEquation`: The plane wave satisfies the wave equation.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The wave equation
- B. Plane wave solutions
  - B.1. Definition of a plane wave
  - B.2. Differentiablity conditions
  - B.3. Time derivatives of plane waves
  - B.4. Space derivatives of plane waves
  - B.5. Laplacian of plane waves
  - B.6. Plane waves satisfy the wave equation
- C. Old lemmas used throughout files

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.WaveEquation
declarations.doc: The general form of the wave equation where `c` is the propagation speed.
declarations.statement:
def WaveEquation {d} (f : Time → Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))
    (t : Time) (x : Space d) (c : ℝ) : Prop

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.planeWave
declarations.doc: A vector-valued plane wave travelling in the direction of `s` with propagation speed `c`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def planeWave (f₀ : ℝ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))
    (c : ℝ) (s : Direction d) : Time → Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.planeWave_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma planeWave_eq {d f₀ c x} {s : Direction d} :
    planeWave f₀ c s t x = f₀ (⟪x, s.unit⟫_ℝ - c * t)

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.planeWave_differentiable_time
ClassicalMechanics.planeWave_differentiable_space
ClassicalMechanics.planeWave_differentiable
ClassicalMechanics.planeWave_time_deriv
ClassicalMechanics.planeWave_time_deriv_time_deriv
ClassicalMechanics.planeWave_space_deriv
declarations.statement:
lemma planeWave_space_deriv {d f₀ c} {s : Direction d}
    (h' : Differentiable ℝ f₀) (i : Fin d) :
    ∂[i] (planeWave f₀ c s t) =
    s.unit i • fun x => planeWave (fderiv ℝ f₀ · 1) c s t x

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.planeWave_apply_space_deriv
declarations.statement:
lemma planeWave_apply_space_deriv {d f₀ c} {s : Direction d}
    (h' : Differentiable ℝ f₀) (i j : Fin d) :
    ∂[i] (fun x => planeWave f₀ c s t x j) =
    s.unit i • fun x => planeWave (fderiv ℝ f₀ · 1) c s t x j

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.planeWave_space_deriv_space_deriv
declarations.statement:
lemma planeWave_space_deriv_space_deriv {d f₀ c} {s : Direction d}
    (h' : ContDiff ℝ 2 f₀) (i : Fin d) :
    ∂[i] (∂[i] (planeWave f₀ c s t)) =
    s.unit i ^ 2 • fun x => planeWave (iteratedDeriv 2 f₀ ·) c s t x

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.planeWave_apply_space_deriv_space_deriv
declarations.statement:
lemma planeWave_apply_space_deriv_space_deriv {d f₀ c} {s : Direction d}
    (h' : ContDiff ℝ 2 f₀) (i j : Fin d) :
    ∂[i] (∂[i] (fun x => planeWave f₀ c s t x j)) =
    (s.unit i) ^ 2 • fun x => planeWave (iteratedDeriv 2 f₀ ·) c s t x j

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.planeWave_laplacian
declarations.statement:
lemma planeWave_laplacian {d f₀ c} {s : Direction d} (h' : ContDiff ℝ 2 f₀) :
    Δᵥ (planeWave f₀ c s t) = fun x => planeWave (iteratedDeriv 2 f₀ ·) c s t x

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.planeWave_waveEquation
declarations.doc: The plane wave satisfies the wave equation.
declarations.statement:
theorem planeWave_waveEquation (c : ℝ) (s : Direction d)
    (f₀ : ℝ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (hf₀ : ContDiff ℝ 2 f₀) :
    ∀ t x, WaveEquation (planeWave f₀ c s) t x c

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.wave_differentiable
declarations.statement:
lemma wave_differentiable {s : Direction d} {c : ℝ} {x : Space d} :
    DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun x => inner ℝ x s.unit - c * t) x

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.wave_dx2
declarations.statement:
lemma wave_dx2 {u v : Fin d} {s : Direction d}
    {f₀' : ℝ → ℝ →L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)} {f₀'' : ℝ → ℝ →L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)}
    (h'' : ∀ x, HasFDerivAt (fun x' => f₀' x' 1) (f₀'' x) x) :
    (fderiv ℝ (fun x' => (inner ℝ ((f₀' (inner ℝ x' s.unit - c * t)) (s.unit u))
    (EuclideanSpace.single v 1))) x) (Space.basis u)
    =
    inner ℝ ((s.unit u) ^ 2 • f₀'' (inner ℝ x s.unit - c * t) 1) (EuclideanSpace.single v 1)

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.space_fderiv_of_inner_product_wave_eq_space_fderiv
declarations.doc:
If `f₀` is a function of `(inner ℝ x s - c * t)`, the fderiv of its components
with respect to spatial coordinates is equal to the corresponding component of
the propagation direction `s` times time derivative.
declarations.statement:
lemma space_fderiv_of_inner_product_wave_eq_space_fderiv
    {t : Time} {f₀ : ℝ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)}
    {s : Direction d} {u v : Fin d} (h' : Differentiable ℝ f₀) :
    c * ((fun x' => (fderiv ℝ (fun x => inner ℝ (f₀ (inner ℝ x s.unit - c * t))
    (EuclideanSpace.single v 1)) x') ((Space.basis u))) x)
    =
    - s.unit u * ∂ₜ (fun t => f₀ (inner ℝ x s.unit - c * t)) t v

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.time_differentiable_of_eq_planewave
ClassicalMechanics.crossProduct_time_differentiable_of_right_eq_planewave
ClassicalMechanics.crossProduct_differentiable_of_right_eq_planewave
ClassicalMechanics.wave_fderiv_inner_eq_inner_fderiv_proj
declarations.statement:
lemma wave_fderiv_inner_eq_inner_fderiv_proj {f₀ : ℝ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)}
    {s : Direction d} {i : Fin d} (h' : Differentiable ℝ f₀) :
    ∀ x y, s.unit i * (fderiv ℝ (fun x => f₀ (inner ℝ x s.unit - c * t)) x) y i
    =
    inner ℝ y s.unit * (fderiv ℝ (fun x => f₀ (inner ℝ x s.unit - c * t) i) x)
    (Space.basis i)

Time-harmonic waves.

Note TODO `EGU3E` may require considerable effort to be made rigorous and may heavily depend on
the status of Fourier theory in Mathlib.

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.WaveVector
declarations.doc: The wavevector which indicates a direction and has magnitude `2π/λ`.
declarations.statement: abbrev WaveVector (d : ℕ := 3)

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.WaveVector.toDirection
declarations.doc: Direction of a wavevector.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def WaveVector.toDirection {d : ℕ} (k : WaveVector d) (h : k ≠ 0) :
    Direction d

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.harmonicWave
declarations.doc: General form of time-harmonic wave in terms of angular frequency `ω` and wave vector `k`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def harmonicWave (a g : ℝ → Space d → ℝ) (ω : WaveVector d → ℝ) (k : WaveVector d) :
    Time → Space d → ℝ

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.transverseHarmonicPlaneWave
declarations.doc:
Transverse monochromatic time-harmonic plane wave where the direction of propagation
is taken to be `EuclideanSpace.single 2 1`. `f₀x` and `f₀y` are the respective amplitudes,
`ω` is the angular frequency, `δx` and `δy` are the respective phases for `fx` and `fy`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def transverseHarmonicPlaneWave (k : WaveVector) (f₀x f₀y ω δx δy : ℝ)
    (hk : k = EuclideanSpace.single 2 (ω/c)) :
    Time → Space → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.transverseHarmonicPlaneWave_eq_planeWave
declarations.doc:
The transverse harmonic planewave representation is equivalent to the general planewave
expression with `‖k‖ = ω/c`.
declarations.statement:
lemma transverseHarmonicPlaneWave_eq_planeWave {c : ℝ} {k : WaveVector} {f₀x f₀y ω δx δy : ℝ}
    (hc_ge_zero : 0 < c) (hω_ge_zero : 0 < ω) (hk : k = EuclideanSpace.single 2 (ω/c)) :
    (transverseHarmonicPlaneWave k f₀x f₀y ω δx δy hk) = planeWave
    (fun p => (f₀x * Real.cos (-(ω/c)*p + δx)) • (EuclideanSpace.single 0 1) +
    (f₀y * Real.cos (-(ω/c)*p + δy)) • (EuclideanSpace.single 1 1)) c
    (WaveVector.toDirection k (by rw [hk]; simp [ne_of_gt, hc_ge_zero, hω_ge_zero]))
